key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines multimodal tool-grounded reasoning with multi-agent actor-critic memory to improve medical question answering across English and seven Indic languages.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical framework for building more equitable healthcare AI systems in low-resource multilingual settings where text-only, English-centric models fail.
method: ArogyaBodha dataset: large-scale multimodal medical QA from 8 sources, spanning 31 body systems, 6 imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains.
ArogyaSutra framework: multi-agent actor-critic design with tool grounding for step-wise reasoning and dual-memory mechanisms for context retention.
Stored actor-critic trajectories are reused for distillation to strengthen reasoning behavior during training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations confirming each component’s contribution.
watch_item: Performance and safety in real clinical use may depend on the quality of tool grounding, language coverage, and robustness to noisy or ambiguous medical inputs.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
